name: Antelopus Selan Oil Exploration
tagline: Debt-free onshore/offshore oil & gas turnaround story with real production growth and a Duarmara discovery surprise -- but the stock already trades near the bull case
verdict_headline: Genuine reserve-to-production execution story (volumes +35-38% CAGR, zero debt, PSC overhang now de-risked) but four_box scores only 2.5 -- thesis_fit retained via the 'growth is un-ignorable' exception, conviction capped at Medium, 'unconfirmed' caveat on valuation
verdict_reasoning: four_box score 2.5 (tailwind yes, tam yes, moat weak, valuation no) would default to 'neither' per the decision table, but invoking the explicit 'growth is un-ignorable' exception: production CAGR ~35-38% roughly matches management's guided delivery, the 2025 Oilfields Regulation & Amendment Act has extended the PSC useful life for Bakrol/Lohar/Cambay by 10 years (removing a known 2030 renewal overhang), and the Duarmara light-oil discovery plus two new DSF Round-IV blocks (Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh) are concrete, dated catalysts -- not a vague story
Per the exception rule, thesis_fit stays 10x-in-2-3-years but conviction is capped at Medium with an explicit 'unconfirmed' caveat, since valuation scored 'no' outright, not just 'weak'

The central caution: FY26 revenue grew only 8% (Rs258.08cr -> Rs278.88cr) despite a 38% 3-year production-volume CAGR -- volume growth has not yet converted into proportional revenue growth, and FY26's 27% PAT growth included a non-recurring ~Rs17.76cr amortization-accounting benefit. At ~43x trailing P/E (richer still if that one-off is excluded), the stock already prices in substantial further execution success

A base-case numeric scenario (see scenario_analysis) implies the current price sits at/slightly above the bull case already -- conviction is capped accordingly rather than raised, despite the genuinely strong operational turnaround
No red flag: zero long-term debt, A/Stable credit rating (Jun 2026), nil promoter pledge, high promoter holding (69.94%) -- red_flag_tier stays CLEAR
business_overview: Antelopus Selan Energy Limited (formerly Selan Exploration Technology, renamed following the 2022-announced, July-2025-effective merger with Antelopus Energy Private Limited) is an Indian onshore/offshore oil & gas exploration and production company. Legacy assets are the Cambay-basin Gujarat fields Bakrol, Lohar and Karjisan (currently ~90% of production), supplemented by the Krishna-Godavari basin Dangeru field (first production Aug-2025) and the Assam Duarmara field, where a 2026 well drilled to target gas in the lower Tipam sands unexpectedly encountered ~37-degree-API light oil in the upper sands -- Duarmara is now the company's single largest 2P reserve asset (19.5 million barrels). Pre-merger Antelopus Energy also holds undeveloped offshore discoveries (Mumbai D-31, Mahanadi D-11) as longer-dated optionality. The company recently won two further onshore blocks under India's DSF Bid Round IV (Cambay basin, Gujarat and Krishna-Godavari basin, Andhra Pradesh). Post-merger management is drawn from Cairn/Vedanta backgrounds with a stated record of running a successful private onshore oil asset in India, and has pursued a self-funded, debt-free growth strategy focused on converting a large (~60 mmboe) 2P reserve base -- against current production of only ~0.5 mmboe/year -- into actual cash flow.

fundamentals_narrative: The operating turnaround is real and reasonably well evidenced: production has grown from 742 boepd (FY24) to a 1,760 boepd exit rate (Q4 FY26), EBITDA margin has expanded from 48% to 58% to ~70% (Q1 FY27) on genuine operating leverage against a largely fixed cost base, the company remains debt-free with an A/Stable rating even while self-funding a multi-field, multi-basin development program, and the 2025 Oilfields Regulation & Amendment Act has extended the PSC useful life for Bakrol/Lohar/Cambay by 10 years, removing what had been a known ~2030 renewal overhang. The Duarmara light-oil discovery and two new DSF Round-IV block wins (Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh) add genuine optionality on top of the legacy fields. The catch is that none of this has yet shown up cleanly on the revenue line: FY26 revenue grew only 8% (Rs258cr -> Rs279cr) even as production volumes grew far faster, implying realization/price and mix have been a headwind that the current ~43x trailing P/E does not obviously discount; and FY26's 27% PAT growth included a non-recurring ~Rs17.76cr amortization-accounting benefit that will not repeat, meaning clean FY27 PAT growth could look materially slower than the headline FY26 number suggests. A numeric bull/base/bear scenario built off the same assumptions (see scenario_analysis) implies the current price already sits at or just above the bull case -- the stock is pricing a clean execution outcome, not offering a margin of safety for one.

Duarmara upper-sands light-oil (37 deg API) discovery disclosed via company announcement/investor presentation during 2026 testing of a well originally targeting lower Tipam-sands gas. Dangeru (KG basin) field commenced first production Aug-2025. Credit rating reaffirmed A/Stable, Jun-2026. No pledge, no auditor resignation, no board/KMP-change red flag found this pass.

Zero long-term debt, A/Stable credit rating, and a fully self-funded Rs250-350cr FY27-28 capex program -- genuinely disciplined capital allocation from a post-merger management team with a strong onshore-oil-asset pedigree (Cairn/Vedanta background)
The 2025 Oilfields Regulation & Amendment Act extended Bakrol/Lohar/Cambay PSC useful life by 10 years, removing the ~2030 renewal overhang that was previously a known risk

Duarmara's upper-sands 37-degree-API light-oil discovery (largest single 2P asset at 19.5 mmbbl) was a genuine positive surprise found while drilling for gas, and two new DSF Round-IV blocks (Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh) add further optionality on top of legacy fields
Against a ~60 mmboe 2P reserve base and current production of only ~0.5 mmboe/year, there is a very long multi-year runway if execution continues to convert reserves into production
bear_case: FY26 revenue grew only 8% (Rs258cr -> Rs279cr) despite a 38% 3-year production-volume CAGR -- volume growth has not yet translated into proportional revenue growth, and the current ~43x trailing P/E does not obviously discount that gap
FY26's 27% PAT growth included a non-recurring ~Rs17.76cr amortization-accounting benefit; clean, like-for-like FY27 PAT growth could look materially slower once that one-off rolls off

A numeric bull/base/bear scenario built off FY26 figures implies the current price already sits at or just above the bull case -- the stock offers little obvious margin of safety if execution disappoints even modestly

Heavy concentration: Bakrol and Karjisan together still account for ~90% of current production; Duarmara's commercial flow rates remain unconfirmed over a sustained period, and the two new DSF IV blocks are pre-exploration with no guaranteed discovery

Commodity price-taker with no pricing power: management itself flags that every $10 Brent decline removes an estimated Rs18-22cr of annual revenue, and crude/USD-INR exposure is a structural, uncontrollable risk

Zero dividend despite consistent profitability -- a defensible reinvestment choice given the reserve-conversion opportunity, but a real zero-direct-return data point worth weighing alongside the other caveats

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: A ~43x trailing multiple for an oil & gas E&P (vs ONGC/Oil India at single-digit-to-low-teens multiples) requires either sustained 30%+ volume-driven EPS growth for several years, or the market crediting the ~60 mmboe reserve base well above where reported earnings currently sit; a reverse-P/E at a cautious 12-15x E&P-appropriate exit multiple would need EPS to roughly triple from here -- a high bar given FY26 revenue grew only 8%
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: Production growth toward the 2,500 boepd exit target is plausible given the FY24-26 delivery record, but revenue/PAT growth likely trails volume growth again unless realization improves; FY26's 27% PAT growth also included a one-off ~Rs17.76cr amortization-accounting benefit that will not repeat, so clean FY27 PAT growth could look materially slower than the FY26 headline suggests
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: A genuine second leg is plausible from Duarmara commercial confirmation, full Dangeru ramp, and DSF IV block appraisal, but these are multi-year, capital-intensive, and unproven at scale
market_expectation.gap_basis: At ~43x trailing P/E (richer still excluding the FY26 one-off accounting benefit), the stock already prices substantial multi-year execution success; FY26's actual revenue growth was only 8% against a 38% 3-year volume CAGR, meaning price/mix realization has been a headwind the current multiple does not obviously discount -- our own numeric scenario build (see scenario_analysis) places the current price at or just above our bull case
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

value_chain.theme: Indian onshore (plus legacy undeveloped offshore) oil & gas E&P, riding India's domestic-production push (~90% import-dependent) and the government's DSF small-field bid-round program
value_chain.position: Licensed operator of legacy Cambay-basin Gujarat fields (Bakrol/Lohar/Karjisan, ~90% of current production) plus newer Assam (Duarmara) and Krishna-Godavari-basin (Dangeru) assets, with two further DSF Round-IV blocks recently won (Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh); undeveloped offshore discoveries (Mumbai D-31, Mahanadi D-11) remain longer-dated optionality

value_chain.note: The moat here is licence/PSC exclusivity (no one else can drill Bakrol/Lohar/Karjisan/Duarmara), not pricing power -- the company remains a pure commodity price-taker on crude realization, with management itself flagging that every $10 Brent move swings annual revenue by an estimated Rs18-22cr.

earnings_quality.normalised_note: Margin expansion from 48% (FY25) to 58% (FY26) to ~70% (Q1 FY27) partly reflects genuine operating leverage on rising volumes, but FY26 PAT was also boosted by a non-recurring ~Rs17.76cr amortization-accounting benefit, and the Q1 FY27 level in particular looks elevated versus what is likely sustainable through a full crude-price cycle; a through-cycle margin in the high-50s/low-60s% range looks more defensible than the ~70% print.

four_box.note: Tailwind (India's domestic-production push + DSF bid-round program) and TAM (~60 mmboe 2P reserves against ~0.5 mmboe/yr current production, plus two new blocks) both genuine. Moat weak (licence/PSC exclusivity is real but the company is a pure commodity price-taker with no pricing power). Valuation downgraded to 'no' (not just 'weak') -- ~43x trailing P/E, richer still excluding the FY26 one-off accounting benefit, with a numeric scenario build placing the current price at or above the bull case. Score 2.5 falls in the 2.0-2.5 band; thesis_fit retained via the written 'growth is un-ignorable' exception (see verdict_reasoning), with conviction capped at Medium and an explicit unconfirmed/valuation caveat rather than upgraded on the strength of the operating story alone.

scenario_analysis.note: Current price (~Rs1,088) sits essentially at or just above our bull-case implied value (~Rs1,027), meaning the market is already paying for a 30% revenue CAGR scenario where volume growth cleanly converts to revenue and margin holds near FY26's elevated, partly one-off-boosted level. The base case -- volume growth continues but revenue/margin normalize more in line with FY26's actual experience (8% revenue growth against 38% volume CAGR) -- implies ~57% downside. Bull requires Duarmara/Dangeru/DSF-IV execution plus favorable crude pricing; bear assumes a reversion toward pre-turnaround economics and a de-rating toward peer-like E&P multiples.
